title: Deleted cart items come back
description: A Dynamo-style store uses N=3, W=2 and R=2. A delete physically removes the key from replicas that receive it. Replica C is cut off for an hour and misses the deletion of cart:42. After it rejoins and nightly Merkle-tree repair runs, the deleted cart comes back. Why did that happen, and what prevents it?

options.text: Anti-entropy treats C's surviving copy as missing data on A and B and re-copies it; write a tombstone on delete and purge it only after a grace period longer than any replica outage.
options.explanation: Without a tombstone, 'absent' on A and B is indistinguishable from 'never received', so repair copies C's old value back. A versioned tombstone wins the comparison, and keeping it longer than the maximum outage window ensures every replica learns of the delete.

options.text: R + W must exceed N + 1; raise W to 3 so deletes reach every replica.
options.explanation: W=3 would make deletes fail whenever any replica is down, violating availability, and still would not help a replica that rejoins with old data after an outage.

options.text: Merkle trees are unreliable for small keys; replace anti-entropy with read repair only.
options.explanation: Read repair would also see C's version as the only existing value and propagate it; and without anti-entropy, cold keys never converge.

options.text: Clock skew on C made its version look newer; switch to vector clocks.
options.explanation: There is no competing newer write to compare against: the delete left nothing behind on A and B, so the version scheme cannot help.
